findings.description: The `.env` read in git-safety has no size limit, and `[ -f ]` follows symlinks. A sandboxed command could make `.env` a sparse 1 TB file, or on Linux a link to `/proc/self/pagemap`, so the read outlasts the 5-second PreToolUse timeout, and a timed-out hook lets the command run. The base branch's sourcing of `.env` was exposed in the same way, and worse, and this PR narrows it. A possible follow-up: refuse a symlinked `.env` and read it through `head -c 65536`, or add "making the read outlast the hook timeout" to decision 34's Cost accepted list.

The `chmodSync(.env, 0o000)` test cannot fail when the suite runs as root, because root ignores the mode and the `.env` names no trunk anyway. This repository's CI runs as the non-root runner user, but in a root container the test passes without reaching the fallback. Skipping it when `process.getuid?.() === 0` would make that visible.

Moving the git-safety paragraph left the `Not closed here` (gate tooling) and `Cursor` bullets under it. Both are about the `.agents/` deny, but they now read as if they qualify the `.env` paragraph. Move the git-safety block below them, or give them their own lead-in.
